title: All-in-Memory Stochastic Computing using ReRAM
problem: Stochastic computing bit-stream generators consume over 80% of system power and area; current solutions focus on gate optimization but ignore high data movement costs between memory and processor for bit-stream exchange.
motivation: Stochastic computing offers fault tolerance and energy efficiency for edge devices, but bit-stream generation is the dominant power bottleneck; in-memory computation can eliminate data movement overhead.
method: The approach performs stochastic computing (calculations using random bit-streams to approximate results) entirely inside ReRAM, a memory type that stores data by changing electrical resistance. Rather than generating random bit-streams in a separate circuit and moving them back and forth to the processor—which wastes power—this system generates random patterns directly in the ReRAM using its natural electrical variation. The same ReRAM cells then do the stochastic calculations and convert results back to ordinary binary numbers. This works because ReRAM naturally tolerates electrical errors, aligning with stochastic computing's design, which remains accurate even with noisy, imperfect data.
key_novelty: Stochastic computing can run entirely within ReRAM memory using the memory's natural electrical variation for randomness, eliminating costly data movement between memory and processor.
contributions: In-place true random number and stochastic bit-stream generation using ReRAM physics

Leverages ReRAM cell variability as inherent randomness source
1.39-2.16× throughput improvement, 1.15-2.8× energy reduction vs CMOS/ReRAM alternatives
5% average image quality drop across multiple tasks
limitations: Limited to image processing tasks; scalability to other SC applications and comparison with recent CMOS designs not discussed.
